# Policies - Absence and Vacation Management

# Last Updated: 2026-08-28

# Purpose

This document defines the process for communicating and managing **employee absences and vacations** within the Candiac branch.

The objective is to ensure absences are properly requested, communicated, and visible to the team so that staffing and daily operations can be planned accordingly.

---

## Objectif

Ce document définit le processus de communication et de gestion des **absences et des vacances des employés** de la succursale de Candiac.

L’objectif est de s’assurer que les absences sont correctement demandées, communiquées et visibles par l’équipe afin de permettre une planification adéquate des effectifs et des opérations quotidiennes.

---

# Planned Absence Procedure

For a planned absence or vacation, follow the steps below.

## Step 1 - Submit the Request

The employee must submit the absence request through:

```text
OnePay

https://onepay.cummins.com/

```

---

## Step 2 - Request Confirmation

The appropriate manager will:

- Review and confirm the request.
- Add the approved absence to the shared **Candiac Branch** calendar.

Once added to the shared calendar, the absence becomes visible to other employees using that calendar.

---

## Step 3 - Notify the Team

On the day before the planned absence, the employee must send an email to the team advising that they will not be present.

The notification should be sent to:

- Technicians
- Office personnel

This ensures that everyone affected by the absence is aware before the employee leaves.

---

# Planned Absence Workflow

```text
Employee Plans Absence
        ↓
Submit Request in OnePay
        ↓
Manager Confirms Request
        ↓
Absence Added to Candiac Branch Calendar
        ↓
Day Before Absence
        ↓
Employee Emails Team
        ↓
Absence
```

---

# Last-Minute Absence

If an employee is sick or encounters an unexpected issue that prevents them from reporting to work:

Contact the appropriate manager directly and advise them of the absence.

The manager will then notify the rest of the team by email.

This process applies to situations where the normal planned absence procedure cannot reasonably be followed.

---

# Candiac Branch Shared Calendar

- Reviewing absence requests.
- Confirming approved requests.
- Adding approved absences to the Candiac Branch shared calendar.
- Communicating unexpected or last-minute absences to the team when required.
- Maintaining visibility of branch staffing through the shared calendar.

---

# Common Mistakes

## Request Submitted but Team Not Notified

Submitting an absence through OnePay does not replace the employee's responsibility to notify the team.

For a planned absence, send the team notification email the day before leaving.

---

## Absence Not Visible on Shared Calendar

Approved planned absences should be added to the **Candiac Branch** shared calendar so the team can account for employee availability.

---

## Last-Minute Absence Not Communicated

For illness or another unexpected absence, contact the appropriate manager as soon as possible so the team can be notified.

---

## Holiday Vacation Requested Too Late

Holiday vacation plans should be established by the end of October.

Requests must also account for the requirement to maintain at least one available employee from each department.

---

## Purpose

This procedure provides Service Coordinators with a simple troubleshooting workflow to guide customers whose generator does not automatically start during a utility power outage and especially during after-hours where sending a technician out to help implies overtime rates.

The objective is to determine whether the issue can be resolved through basic operator actions before dispatching a technician in regular day-hours rather than after-hours.

> **Important**
>
> This procedure is intended for basic customer troubleshooting only.
>
> This procedure is intended for Cummins/Onan generators only.
>
> Customers should never perform work that exposes them to electrical hazards or unsafe conditions.
>
> If at any point the customer is uncomfortable performing a step, discontinue the procedure and schedule service.

Cette procédure fournit aux coordonnateurs de service un flux de dépannage simple pour guider les clients dont le générateur ne démarre pas automatiquement lors d'une panne de courant du réseau électrique, en particulier en dehors des heures normales, où l'envoi d'un technicien implique des tarifs de temps supplémentaire.

L'objectif est de déterminer si le problème peut être résolu par des actions de base de l'opérateur avant de dépêcher un technicien pendant les heures normales de la journée plutôt qu'en dehors des heures normales.

>
> Cette procédure est destinée uniquement au dépannage de base par le client.

> Cette procédure est destinée uniquement aux générateurs Cummins/Onan.

> Les clients ne doivent jamais effectuer de travaux les exposant à des risques électriques ou à des conditions dangereuses.

> Si, à tout moment, le client se sent mal à l'aise d'exécuter une étape, interrompre la procédure et planifier une intervention de service.

# Information to Collect Before Dispatch

If a technician will be dispatched, collect as much information as possible from the customer.

Recommended information includes:

- Active fault code
- Alarm description
- Whether the generator started manually
- Whether the reset procedure was attempted
- Any unusual observations

Examples:

- Low Coolant
- High Engine Temperature
- FC1223
- Emergency Stop active

This information assists the Service Coordinator in selecting the appropriate technician and preparing the service call.

---

# Safety Reminders

Advise the customer to stop the procedure immediately if:

- Smoke is present.
- Fire is present.
- Fuel is leaking.
- Electrical hazards are observed.
- The generator appears unsafe to operate.

In these situations:

- Do not continue troubleshooting.
- Arrange for immediate service.

---

# Best Practices

- Record any fault codes before scheduling service.
- Walk through each troubleshooting step in order.
- Keep the customer informed throughout the process.
- Escalate the call if the generator cannot be safely restarted.

---

# Common Mistakes

## Selector Not Left in AUTO

A generator cannot automatically respond to a power outage unless the controller is left in **AUTO** mode.

---

## Alarm Reset Skipped

Always attempt a basic alarm reset before proceeding to manual start when an alarm is present.

---

## Repeated Start Attempts

Repeatedly attempting to start the generator without identifying the underlying fault may worsen the situation.

If the generator does not start after the basic procedure, schedule service.

---

## Missing Fault Information

Whenever possible, record any displayed alarm or fault code before dispatching a technician.

This information greatly improves troubleshooting efficiency.

results.question: An airport has no current outage, but preventive maintenance is overdue and the customer has a service window. How should I prepare this service call before assigning and confirming a technician?

run.answer:
Treat this as a preventive-maintenance job, not an outage response. Before assigning a technician:

1. Confirm customer/account status, contract requirements, and billing coverage.
2. Verify the PM scope and that the service window is confirmed with the airport contact.
3. Check whether the PM has already been rescheduled:
   - Each reschedule raises priority by one level.
   - After two reschedules, supervisor approval is required to postpone again.
   - A PM can reach P3 but does not take priority over an equipment failure.
4. Confirm the generator/site details, operating hours, airport access/security requirements, parking, safety restrictions, and an accessible on-site contact.
5. Confirm any required parts/materials are available; do not schedule work dependent on unavailable parts without approval.
6. Obtain/document required customer approval under the applicable contract or quotation process.
7. Create or update the BMS/FieldAware record with the unit/site, PM scope, service window, contacts, access notes, coverage/billing, and required documents.
8. In BMS, associate the correct unit and site, use the appropriate market segment (**SOLUTIONS** for PM contract; **STANDBY** without a contract), set Primary Failure Measure to **HOURS**, and build the job plan.

Then select a technician who can meet the airport window and site-access requirements, reserve the appointment, complete the pre-dispatch review, and confirm with the customer.

# 1. Gather Essential Information

Use the following questions during the call. Record the answers in the applicable customer and work-order records.

## Customer and Account

- Whether a site contact or network will be available if the technician needs assistance. Explain that a technician cannot be expected to work alone; if no person is readily accessible and no suitable on-site network is available, the work may be refused.

## Equipment

- Manufacturer and model.
- Serial number or nameplate information.
- Current operating hours, when available.
- Generator location and access details.

## Problem Description

Ask:

- Is an alarm or fault code displayed? Record the exact code and description.
- What happened, and when did it start?
- Will the generator start or operate?
- Are there visible symptoms such as a coolant leak, smoke, or a battery problem?

Examples include `FC1223` and `Low Coolant`.

For inverter (ATS)-related issues, confirm whether a simulated outage can be performed and what time window is suitable.

# Alarm Classification

## Purpose

An alarm or fault does **not** have an intrinsic priority.

Its urgency is determined by its **impact on the availability of the equipment**, not simply by the alarm code itself.

The dispatcher must determine how the alarm affects the generator before assigning a priority.

---

# Alarm Levels

| Alarm Level | Definition | Typical Priority |
|--------------|------------|------------------|
| **Blocking Alarm** | The generator cannot start or cannot accept load. Examples include active shutdowns, failed start attempts, ATS transfer failures, or any condition that makes the unit unavailable. | **P1** for C1–C2 customers without redundancy or with safety impact; **P2** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Reliability Alarm** | The generator continues to operate but its ability to support a future outage is compromised. Examples include battery charger failures, low fuel level, defective block heater, coolant leak, etc. | **P2** for C1–C2 customers; **P3** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Minor Alarm** | No immediate impact on equipment availability. Examples include sensor faults, reminder lamps, or maintenance notifications. | Service Call (Non-Urgent): **P3** (C1–C3) or **P5** (C4). |

---

# Dispatcher Decision Process

The primary question is:

> **If utility power fails right now, will the generator start and carry the load?**

| Answer | Alarm Classification |
|---------|----------------------|
| No, or uncertain | Blocking Alarm |
| Yes, but with increased risk | Reliability Alarm |
| Yes, with no significant risk | Minor Alarm |

This single question should guide the initial classification before determining the final priority.

---

# Additional Considerations

Alarm classification should also consider the probability that the equipment could fail before the next maintenance opportunity.

Factors may include:

- Oil pressure
- Engine temperature
- Fuel level
- Battery condition
- Coolant leaks
- Site redundancy
- Whether the entire facility depends on the generator
- Criticality of the customer's operation

The coordinator should ask enough questions to determine whether the generator is:

- Completely shut down (`Shutdown`)
- Operating with reduced reliability (`Warning`)
- Operating normally with only informational notifications

---

# Typical Shutdown Conditions

A preventive maintenance activity that reaches **P3** becomes equivalent to a typical non-urgent service call but never reaches the priority of an equipment failure.

Once a PM has been rescheduled twice, it may not be postponed again without supervisor approval.

Each reschedule increases the priority by one level. No preventive maintenance activity should be postponed more than two times.

---

## Rule 5 — Customer Ranking

When two jobs have the same Priority Level and the same Client Class, customer ranking is used as the final business tie-breaker.

Use this report when a user asks for the best, top, or highest-ranked customers/clients, particularly when customer sales or margin ranking is being used as a dispatch tie-breaker.

# Part 2 - Associate the Unit and Site

Select the **Unit / Products** tab and associate the correct existing generator unit.

1. Open the Unit lookup.
2. Verify the serial number, model, and existing unit details.

# Part 3 - Build the Job Plan

Select the **Job Plan** tab. The Job Plan determines the labor allocation quoted and later billed.

## Required SRTs

Every standard mobile service call begins with:

- **99-999 - NON-SRT DETAIL**
- **99-990 - TRAVEL**

To retrieve an SRT:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Load SRTs For Group | **99** |
| Procedure | **999** or **990** |
| Of Qty | **1** |

Select **Retrieve** for each required SRT.

## Four-Hour Rule

A standard mobile service call is quoted as a minimum of **4.0 labor hours**. Adjust the SRT quantities so the total allocation meets the applicable minimum and reflects the expected travel and work.

Review the Job Plan before converting the WOQT:

- Send the 750-hour maintenance parts list to Jean-François.
- Plan approximately two technicians for two days.

- Confirm the required 750-hour maintenance parts.

# Part 4 - Add Miscellaneous Charges

Open **Total WO**, then select **Misc Charges**.

## Mileage

Select `KILOMETRES` in the **Name** field and enter the round-trip distance calculated with Google Maps.

Use the applicable starting point:

- North Shore: assigned storage unit to customer site.
- Montreal region: Candiac Branch to customer site.
- National Capital Region: Ottawa Branch to customer site.

The standard mileage rate is currently **$3.25/km**. Verify current rates in [Service Billing Rates](../reference/service_hourly_rates.md).

Enter the appropriate tax district and save the Misc Charges record.

- Round-trip distance was used.

# Part 5 - Convert the WOQT to a WO

After the quotation is complete and approval requirements are satisfied:

1. Select **Quote => WO** beside Transaction Type.
2. At **Accept / Reject Quote**, select **Accept**.
3. If BMS displays a tax-district warning, select **Yes** only after confirming the correct tax district and billing arrangement.

Creating the WOQT first:

- Allows customer approval of pricing.
- Ensures labor and travel are quoted correctly.

# Part 6 - Pre-Scheduling Verification

Before finalizing the technician assignment and appointment:

- Confirm the Complaint contains enough information about the work or generator issue.
- Confirm the Work Order contact is the person who communicated the request.
- Confirm the on-site contact name and phone number are included.
- Verify that customer credit is sufficient for the job.
- If credit is insufficient, obtain the required approval before proceeding.
- Verify that required parts are available or confirm an approved alternative.
- Select an appropriate tentative time slot in FieldAware.
- Contact the selected technician when required to review the issue and confirm suitability.
- Confirm the proposed appointment with the customer.

For quotation preparation and approval, use [Preparing and Accepting a Quote](../procedures/quote_management.md).

This mechanism prevents preventive maintenance from remaining indefinitely in the backlog.

## Step 5 — Service Call

**Question**

> Is this a service call?

### Decision

| Customer Class | Priority |
|----------------|----------|
| C1–C3 | P3 |
| C4 / Residential | P5 |

## Step 6 — Preventive Maintenance

**Question**

> Is this a preventive maintenance activity?

### Decision

Critical preventive maintenance receives:

- Five-year maintenance
- Monthly maintenance
- Customer-committed maintenance windows
- Annual CSA maintenance

→ **P4**

Routine preventive maintenance receives:

- Annual maintenance
- Full inspection
- Generator inspection

→ **P6**

---

# Client Class Assignment

Once the Priority Level has been determined, the Client Class is assigned according to the Client Classification rules.

The final prioritization code is generated as:

```text
P#-C#
```

Examples:

- P1-C1
- P2-C3
- P4-C2

---

# Comparison with Existing Work

After generating the prioritization code, the job is compared against all existing scheduled work using the comparison rules documented in:

- **Comparison Rules**

The comparison is always performed from left to right:

1. Priority Level
2. Client Class
3. Job Type
4. Customer Ranking (when applicable)
5. Additional business tie-breakers

---

# Relationship to the Prioritization Engine

This document describes the business decision process used to determine a job's priority.

The interactive Prioritization Engine implements this process by presenting the appropriate questions to the user, evaluating the responses according to the documented business rules, and automatically generating the corresponding prioritization code.

The software implementation may evolve over time, but any changes to the decision logic should remain consistent with the business rules documented in this repository.

# Last Updated: 2026-09-11

# Bank of Canada — Security Access

## Purpose

This procedure explains the security screening process that must be completed for an employee or technician who requires access to a **Bank of Canada (BoC) site**.

Bank of Canada security screening is separate from security clearances obtained for other government buildings. An employee who is already cleared to enter another government facility **cannot use that clearance as authorization to access a Bank of Canada site**.

---

## Source Document

The complete Bank of Canada security screening instructions are available here:

**Source document:** [Bank of Canada Security Screening Instructions](https://cummins365-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/ud016_cummins_com/IQAT5Bccq0NaSoMAFkOsofWaARmvZBsF5YEdpQFG0mErnaU?e=FqD2u4)

---

## Security Screening Process

### 1. Personal Information Request (PIR)

A **Personal Information Request (PIR)** form will be sent to the employer or employee requiring access.

The individual requiring access must:

1. Complete the PIR form.
2. Send the completed form to:
   **facilities-RFA@bank-banque-canada.ca**
3. Include:
   - the Bank of Canada site location for which access is required;
   - the expected frequency of access.

---

### 2. Mintz Screening Invitation

After the PIR has been submitted, allow **up to 48 hours** to receive the Mintz screening invitation.

The Mintz invitation may be delivered to the employee's **spam or junk folder**, so these folders should be checked if the invitation does not appear in the main inbox.

If no Mintz invitation has been received within 48 hours, including in spam/junk folders, contact:

**facilities-RFA@bank-banque-canada.ca**

for assistance.

### Important — Mintz Expiration

The Mintz invitation must be completed **within 10 days of receiving it**.

If it is not completed within 10 days, the invitation will be cancelled and a **new Mintz submission will be required**.

---

### 3. Fingerprints — If Requested

After passing the Mintz screening, the employee may be asked to provide fingerprints to assist with identification.

results.question: Help. A customer reports an intermittent PCC3300 alarm after a breaker transfer while an ATS transitions under load. What do I need to clarify before deciding what to do or dispatching a technician?

run.answer:
Before deciding priority or dispatch, clarify:

- **Exact PCC3300 alarm/fault code and full text**, whether it is active or history, and when it clears.
- **Generator availability:** If utility fails now, will it auto-start, transfer, and carry load? Did it successfully carry load during the reported event?
- **Effect of the alarm:** shutdown/blocking, warning/reliability concern, or informational only; any failed starts, breaker-trip/open commands, or ATS transfer failures.
- **Event sequence:** utility-to-generator or generator-to-utility transfer; open-, closed-, or delayed-transition ATS; whether the alarm occurs before, during, or after transfer.
- **ATS details:** ATS make/model, active alarms, position/status indications, and whether transfer under load completed normally.
- **Load/site conditions:** load magnitude/type, unusual load steps, parallel equipment, and whether the issue repeats consistently or only intermittently.
- **Safety conditions:** smoke, fire, fuel leak, electrical hazard, overheating, abnormal noise, or visible damage. If present, stop troubleshooting and arrange immediate service.
- **Customer impact:** facility criticality, redundancy, and customer class (C1–C4), since priority is based on equipment availability and impact—not the alarm code alone.
- **History/actions:** prior occurrences, recent maintenance/configuration/ATS work, manual-reset or restart attempts, and any photos/event logs.

Decision basis: if the generator cannot reliably start, transfer, or accept load—or that is uncertain—treat it as a **blocking alarm**. If it still supports the load but future outage reliability is compromised, classify it as a **reliability alarm**. Record the PCC and ATS information before dispatch; an intermittent PCC/ATS transfer-under-load issue may require a technician experienced in controls and ATS diagnostics.

# Alarm Classification

## Purpose

An alarm or fault does **not** have an intrinsic priority.

Its urgency is determined by its **impact on the availability of the equipment**, not simply by the alarm code itself.

The dispatcher must determine how the alarm affects the generator before assigning a priority.

---

# Alarm Levels

| Alarm Level | Definition | Typical Priority |
|--------------|------------|------------------|
| **Blocking Alarm** | The generator cannot start or cannot accept load. Examples include active shutdowns, failed start attempts, ATS transfer failures, or any condition that makes the unit unavailable. | **P1** for C1–C2 customers without redundancy or with safety impact; **P2** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Reliability Alarm** | The generator continues to operate but its ability to support a future outage is compromised. Examples include battery charger failures, low fuel level, defective block heater, coolant leak, etc. | **P2** for C1–C2 customers; **P3** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Minor Alarm** | No immediate impact on equipment availability. Examples include sensor faults, reminder lamps, or maintenance notifications. | Service Call (Non-Urgent): **P3** (C1–C3) or **P5** (C4). |

---

# Dispatcher Decision Process

The primary question is:

> **If utility power fails right now, will the generator start and carry the load?**

| Answer | Alarm Classification |
|---------|----------------------|
| No, or uncertain | Blocking Alarm |
| Yes, but with increased risk | Reliability Alarm |
| Yes, with no significant risk | Minor Alarm |

This single question should guide the initial classification before determining the final priority.

---

# Additional Considerations

Alarm classification should also consider the probability that the equipment could fail before the next maintenance opportunity.

Factors may include:

- Oil pressure
- Engine temperature
- Fuel level
- Battery condition
- Coolant leaks
- Site redundancy
- Whether the entire facility depends on the generator
- Criticality of the customer's operation

The coordinator should ask enough questions to determine whether the generator is:

- Completely shut down (`Shutdown`)
- Operating with reduced reliability (`Warning`)
- Operating normally with only informational notifications

results.question: Comment créer un bon de travail dans BMS et quelles informations dois-je vérifier?

run.answer:
Selon la procédure BMS :

1. **Créer d’abord une soumission de BT (WOQT)** — ne créez pas directement le WO.
2. Remplir les informations client et du bon de travail.
3. Sélectionner l’**unité** et le **site** existants; les créer au besoin.
4. Compléter le **plan de travail (Job Plan)**, incluant les SRT applicables et les frais divers, par exemple le kilométrage.
5. Obtenir l’approbation de prix, puis **convertir le WOQT en WO**.
6. Avant l’envoi à FieldAware, vérifier :
   - le crédit du client;
   - la disponibilité des pièces;
   - le technicien requis;
   - la date et l’heure de rendez-vous;
   - l’exactitude des informations client, unité, site et travail demandé.
7. Enregistrer le WO et sélectionner **Send to FA**.
8. Dans FieldAware, assigner le technicien comme *Job Lead*, planifier la durée, attribuer les rapports requis (Field Service Basic et RFQ), puis vérifier l’horaire dans le Scheduler.

Après tout changement important dans BMS, utilisez de nouveau **Send to FA** afin d’éviter que les modifications non synchronisées soient écrasées.

results.question: How do I create a work order in BMS?

run.answer:
### Create a BMS Work Order

1. **Open a new Work Order** in BMS.
2. Create it first as a quotation:
   - **Service Location:** Candiac **Z8** or Ottawa **AK**
   - **Customer Number**
   - **Work Order Type:** `Mobile`
   - **Transaction Type:** `WOQT`
   - Appropriate subtype
   - Requester/contact and on-site contact details
   - Customer PO, if required
   - Payment type: `CHARGE` or `COD / CASH`

3. Complete the work-order sections:
   - **Complaint:** Issue, fault codes, on-site contact, access and safety details
   - **Cause:** `To be determined.`
   - **Coverage:** `Customer Billable`, unless documented otherwise
   - **Correction:** `To be filled once the work has been performed by the technician.`
   - **Remarks:**  
     `Thank you for choosing Cummins.`  
     `Quote may vary once work has been completed.`
   - Enter the responsible supervisor/coordinator.

4. Select or create the correct **Unit and Site**.

5. Complete the **Job Plan, SRT allocation, miscellaneous charges, and round-trip mileage**.

6. Save the WOQT and obtain customer approval.

7. **Convert the WOQT to a live WO** after approval.

8. Before scheduling, verify:
   - Customer credit/payment requirements
   - Parts availability
   - Suitable technician
   - Appointment date
   - Known safety concerns

9. Record the technician and service date in **STATUS**, save, then select **Send to FA**.

10. Finish technician assignment, scheduling, and report assignment in FieldAware. Confirm the job appears under the correct technician and date in the Scheduler.

Select **Send to FA after every later BMS modification** so FieldAware does not overwrite the change.

# BMS - Overtime Entry

# Last Updated: 2026-09-03

## Purpose

This document explains how Service Coordinators must enter **overtime (OT)** in BMS when preparing quotations or completing invoicing.

Correctly charging overtime ensures that customer quotations and invoices accurately reflect labor costs and comply with branch billing practices.

## Objectif

Ce document explique comment les coordonnateurs de service doivent entrer les **heures supplémentaires (OT)** dans BMS lors de la préparation des soumissions ou de la facturation.

La saisie correcte des heures supplémentaires permet de s’assurer que les soumissions et les factures reflètent fidèlement les coûts de main-d’œuvre et respectent les pratiques de facturation de la succursale.

---

# When to Apply Overtime

Overtime must be entered whenever a technician works **more than 8 regular hours in a single day**.

Hours exceeding the first 8 regular hours must be charged using the appropriate overtime rate.

## Example

A technician works **10 hours**.

The labor should be entered as:

- 8 hours → Regular Time (RT)
- 2 hours → Overtime (OT)

Do **not** enter all 10 hours as regular time.

---

# Where to Perform This Step

This procedure is completed in the **Job Plan** tab within **BMS**.

It applies to:

- Customer quotations
- Customer invoicing

Whenever overtime is applicable, the coordinator must update the Job Plan accordingly.

---

# Entering Overtime in BMS

## Step 1

Enter the first **8 hours** using the normal labor operation lines.

Typical examples include:

- 88 ADM 00 902
- 88 JSA
- 99 999
- 99 990

These represent the technician's regular labor.

---

## Step 2

After the first 8 hours have been entered, create an **additional Job Plan line**.

This additional line is used exclusively for overtime hours.

Do not modify the regular labor line.

---

## Step 3

For the overtime entry:

Access:

```text
99 999
```

Access Type:

```text
R
```

Rate Type:

```text
FSOT
```

Enter only the hours worked beyond the initial 8 regular hours.

---

# Overtime Rate

The **Rate** field is **not populated automatically**.

Coordinators must manually enter the correct hourly rate.

Use the current service rate sheets available on the departmental Teams site.

Examples include:

- Candiac Mobile Service Rates
- Ottawa Mobile Service Rates
- Candiac In-Shop Rates
- Ottawa In-Shop Rates

Always verify that the rate corresponds to the branch and service type before saving.

---

# Example

Technician works:

**10 hours**

The Job Plan should contain:

| Labor Type | Hours |
|------------|------:|
| Regular Time | 8.0 |
| FSOT | 2.0 |

---

# Coordinator Responsibilities

Before saving the quotation or invoice:

- Verify whether total labor exceeds 8 hours.
- Split regular and overtime hours correctly.
- Create a separate Job Plan line for overtime.
- Select **FSOT** as the overtime rate type.
- Manually enter the correct overtime rate using the current rate sheet.
- Verify the final labor totals before completing the quotation or invoice.

---

# Common Mistakes

## Charging All Hours as Regular Time

Incorrect:

```text
10 hours RT
```

Correct:

```text
8 hours RT
2 hours FSOT
```

---

## Forgetting to Add a Separate Job Plan Line

Overtime must always be entered on its own Job Plan line.

---

## Incorrect Rate Type

Always use:

```text
FSOT
```

for overtime entries.

---

## Incorrect Hourly Rate

Do not rely on BMS to populate the overtime rate.

The coordinator must manually enter the appropriate rate using the current branch rate sheet.

---

# Best Practices

- Review technician labor hours before completing every quotation or invoice.
- Apply overtime consistently whenever labor exceeds 8 hours.
- Confirm the correct overtime rate before saving the Job Plan.
- Double-check the quotation or invoice after entering overtime.

results.question: How do I create a FieldAware work order?

run.answer:
A FieldAware job is created by synchronizing a completed BMS Work Order.

1. Create and save the quote as a **WOQT in BMS**.
2. Obtain customer approval and convert the WOQT to a live Work Order.
3. Verify customer credit, parts availability, technician, and appointment details.
4. In BMS, select **Send to FA**.
5. Record the generated **FA Job ID**.
6. In FieldAware, search for and open that Job ID.
7. Assign the technician as **Job Lead**.
8. Enter the appointment date, time, and duration.
9. Assign **Field Service Basic** and **Request for Quote (RFQ)** reports.
10. Remove unnecessary reports and assign the technician to every remaining report.
11. Save and verify the job appears correctly in the **Scheduler**.

Use **Send to FA** again after every material BMS change; otherwise, unsynchronized changes may be overwritten.

| Branch | Code |
|---|---|
| Candiac | **Z8** |
| Ottawa | **AK** |

### Customer

Enter the customer’s **Customer Number**. If the customer does not exist, create the customer account before continuing.

### Work Order Type

For a standard mobile service call, select:

```text
Mobile
```

### Transaction Type

Enter:

```text
WOQT
```

### Subtype

Select the subtype that best represents the work, such as:

- FSPG
- FSONPG
- PMR ASAP
- PMR EMERGENT

### Contact

Enter the person who communicated the service request. Confirm the on-site contact name and phone number are also documented in the Complaint or applicable work-order fields.

### Purchase Order (PO)

Enter the customer’s PO when available or required. The PO is the only value that can still be modified after invoicing.

### Payment Type

Select the applicable payment type, such as:

- **CHARGE** - Customer has an approved credit account.
- **COD / CASH** - Payment is required according to the cash-customer procedure.

For cash customers, follow [Cash Customers - Service Call](../procedures/cash_customers_service_call.md) or [Cash Customers - Accepted Quotation](../procedures/cash_customers_accepted_quote.md).

## Complete the Work-Order Sections

### Complaint

Summarize the customer’s issue and include:

- Problem description and customer observations.
- Alarm or fault codes.
- On-site contact name and phone number.
- Relevant access, safety, or site information.

Example:

```text
Generator displays FC1223 Low Coolant alarm.
Customer reports unit shuts down approximately 20 minutes after starting.
On-Site Contact: John Smith, 514-555-1234
```

### Cause

Before inspection, enter:

```text
To be determined.
```

The technician or coordinator completes the Cause after troubleshooting.

### Coverage

For standard customer-billable work, select:

```text
Customer Billable
```

Select warranty or another coverage only when supported by the applicable documentation.

### Correction

Before work is completed, enter:

```text
To be filled once the work has been performed by the technician.
```

### Remarks

Use the standard customer message when applicable:

```text
Thank you for choosing Cummins.
Quote may vary once work has been completed.
```

### Supervisor

Enter the responsible coordinator or supervisor according to branch practice.

## Save the WOQT

After the required fields are complete:

For non-Cummins equipment, explain that a technician may be available, but may not specialize in that product; referral to a more specialized provider may be necessary.

# 2. Classify the Request

Determine the primary job type:

- Service call or troubleshooting.
- Preventive maintenance.
- Project work, installation, commissioning, upgrade, or major repair.
- Inspection.
- Parts-only request.

Route parts-only requests according to [Front Desk Call Triage](front_desk_call_triage.md). Use the applicable Service or PM workflow for technician work.

# 3. Confirm Customer and Work Requirements

Before scheduling or dispatching, confirm the requirements that apply to the job.

## Customer Status

- Charge customer: verify the customer account and credit status according to branch practice.
- Cash customer: follow the appropriate cash-customer procedure before dispatch or ordering parts.
- Contract or special customer: verify the applicable agreement and service requirements.

See:

- [Cash Customers - Overview](cash_customers_overview.md)
- [Cash Customers - Service Call](cash_customers_service_call.md)
- [Cash Customers - Accepted Quotation](cash_customers_accepted_quote.md)

## Parts and Materials

Confirm at a high level:

- Whether parts are required.
- Whether parts are available or already ordered.
- Expected delivery timing when parts are missing.
- Whether the appointment should wait for parts.

Do not schedule work that depends on unavailable parts unless the appropriate approval has been obtained.

## Customer Approval

Before dispatch, confirm that the customer has approved the work through the applicable method, such as:

- Signed quotation.
- Written email approval.
- Other documented approval accepted by branch practice.

Use [Preparing and Accepting a Quote](quote_management.md) for the quotation and approval workflow.

# 4. Prepare the Records

Create or update the applicable BMS and FieldAware records with enough information for the technician and the next coordinator to understand the job.

At a minimum, ensure that the records include:

- Customer and on-site contact information.
- Equipment identification and location.
- Clear complaint or symptom description.
- Alarm or fault codes.
- Site access and safety information.
- Coverage or billing status.
- Required reports and supporting documents.

Use [BMS - Work Order Creation](../software/bms_work_order_creation.md) for detailed WOQT, work-order, billing-field, and synchronization instructions.

# Clover - Invoice to Pay

# Last Updated: 2026-09-02

## Purpose

This procedure explains how to use **Clover Invoice to Pay** to send a customer an email payment link.

The customer uses the link to enter their own payment information directly in Clover, avoiding the need to provide credit card information over the phone or by email.

## Objectif

Cette procédure explique comment utiliser **Clover Invoice to Pay** afin d'envoyer au client un lien de paiement par courriel.

Le client peut ainsi saisir lui-même ses informations de paiement directement dans Clover, sans avoir à transmettre ses informations de carte de crédit par téléphone ou par courriel.

---

## Quick Reference / Référence rapide

**Clover Invoice to Pay / Clover Invoice / Payment Link / Lien de paiement**

Clover Invoice to Pay allows a customer to receive an invoice by email and complete the payment directly through Clover.

General workflow:

```text
Log into Clover
        ↓
Open Virtual Terminal or Invoices
        ↓
Create New Invoice
        ↓
Enter Amount
        ↓
Enter Invoice / Order Number
        ↓
Select or Create Customer
        ↓
Create Invoice
        ↓
Customer Receives Email
        ↓
Customer Selects Pay
        ↓
Customer Completes Payment
        ↓
Monitor Invoice Status in Clover
```

### French Retrieval Concepts

- Clover Invoice to Pay
- Facture Clover
- Paiement Clover
- Lien de paiement
- Lien de paiement Clover
- Envoyer un lien de paiement
- Paiement par courriel
- Facture par courriel
- Client paie lui-même
- Paiement carte de crédit sans téléphone
- Paiement carte de crédit sans courriel
- Envoyer une facture Clover

---

# Accessing Invoice to Pay

Log into Clover.

From the landing page, select either:

- **Virtual Terminal**
- **Invoices**

Both options can be used to access the invoice creation process.

---

# Creating an Invoice

## Via Virtual Terminal

Access the invoice functionality through the **Virtual Terminal**.

## Via Invoices

1. Select **Invoice** from the Transaction Type drop-down.
2. Select **Create New Invoice**.

Either method will take you to the Clover **Invoice** page.

---

# Entering Invoice Information

On the Invoice page:

No parts should be ordered and work should not proceed until the required payment has been received.

---

# Clover Payment

For an accepted cash quotation:

```text
Full Quotation Amount = Payment
```

Do **not** use a Clover pre-authorization.

Collect the full amount of the accepted quotation.

After processing the payment:

- Retrieve the payment receipt.
- Send the receipt to the customer.

Refer to **Clover Training** for the detailed Clover payment procedure.

---

# Customer Deposit / Order Entry

After the full payment has been received, process the amount using the applicable **Customer Deposit / Order Entry (OE)** procedure.

The OE is used to reserve and apply the customer's payment against the Work Order.

Refer to the **Customer Deposits Process** for the complete BMS deposit and OE workflow.

---

# Dispatch and Work

Parts may be ordered and work may proceed once:

- The full quotation amount has been received.
- The required customer deposit / OE process has been completed.

Continue using the standard Work Order and scheduling procedures.

---

# Post-Service Follow-Up

After the work has been completed:

- Follow up with the assigned supervisor.
- Verify that the technician's labor/punch has been entered.
- Confirm that the Work Order is identified as a * cash customer**.

Contact the customer to:

- Confirm that the service has been completed.
- Explain the work performed.
- Review the final amount.
- Answer any customer questions.
- Confirm customer satisfaction.

---

# Final Payment

For an accepted cash quotation, the quoted amount has **already been paid before the work begins**.

After the work is completed:

- Verify the final amount.
- Confirm that the previously collected payment has been properly applied.
- Address any additional approved billable amount when applicable.

Unlike a standard cash service call, there is no pre-authorization to convert into payment.

---

# Final Invoice and Documentation

The final invoice should be produced and sent during the **same week the work was completed**.

Send the customer:

- Final invoice.
- Payment receipt, if not previously provided.

When all information is complete and the billing values are reconciled:

1. Confirm that a PO has been entered when required.
2. Select the **Close** checkbox.
3. Enter the required security code.
4. Save the invoice/work order.

Do not close the work order while required reports, cause information, coverage, SRTs, charges, approval, or customer information are incomplete.

# 7. Deliver the Invoice

Follow the applicable delivery method.

## HighRadius-Generated Invoice

If HighRadius generates and delivers the invoice, no additional manual email is required unless branch or customer requirements specify otherwise.

## Manual Email Delivery

If the invoice must be sent manually:

1. Open the customer lookup/contact setup in BMS.
2. Select the customer and choose **Setup**.
3. Confirm that the customer’s email address is present and correct.
4. If it is missing, obtain the address from the customer and add it to the contact record.
5. Save the contact record with **F10**, when applicable.
6. Use **Send to FA** when required to synchronize the updated contact information.
7. Save and send the invoice by email.

### Email Format

Subject:

```text
[Invoice Number]
```

Include:

- A brief description or summary of the work.
- The invoice or required attachment.
- A professional thank-you to the customer.

Example structure:

```text
Subject: Invoice 123456

Hello [Customer],

Please find attached the invoice for [brief description of work].

Thank you for choosing Cummins.
```

Confirm that the invoice was sent to the correct customer email address.

# 8. Filing and Follow-Up

After delivery:

- Confirm that the invoice is closed in BMS.
- Confirm that the work order and FieldAware records are synchronized where required.
- File or retain supporting reports and approval documentation according to branch practice.
- If payment remains outstanding, follow the applicable customer or cash-customer process.

For cash customers, use [Cash Customers - Service Call](cash_customers_service_call.md) or [Cash Customers - Accepted Quotation](cash_customers_accepted_quote.md).

For a credit against an already invoiced work order, use [Customer Invoice Credit](customer_invoice_credit.md).

## Common Mistakes

1. Enter the payment amount.
2. Enter the applicable **invoice or order number** in the **Note** field.

---

# Selecting the Customer

Add a new customer or locate an existing customer.

Once the customer has been selected, the **Create Invoice** button becomes available.

Select the appropriate delivery options when required.

Then select:

```text
Create Invoice
```

---

# Customer Payment

After the invoice has been created, the customer receives an email from Clover.

The customer selects the:

```text
Pay
```

link contained in the email.

This opens the Clover payment page.

The customer then enters their own payment information and completes the transaction directly through Clover.

---

# Monitoring the Invoice

To review existing invoices:

1. Select **Invoices** from the left-hand menu.
2. Locate the applicable invoice.

The Invoices page displays the current status of the invoice.

Additional invoice functions are available through the **three-dot menu** located on the right side of the invoice.

---

The official **Clover Invoice to Pay** SharePoint document contains the complete visual procedure, including screenshots showing invoice creation, customer selection, the customer email, the Pay link, payment page, and invoice status management.

results.question: Give me an overview of the warranty claim process.

run.answer:
## Warranty Claim Process Overview

1. **Identify the correct warranty path**
   - **Distributor Warranty:** Covered through the distributor arrangement.
   - **Generator Engine—CECO:** Failed component belongs to the engine; verify through QuickServe Online.
   - **Generator—Onan:** Failed component belongs to the generator; verify through PGBU.
   - **Electric Bus—CECO:** Use QuickServe and the Electrification Failure Code Manual.

2. **Collect required information**
   - ESN or unit serial number
   - Verified Date in Service/Warranty Start Date
   - Hours or mileage
   - Failed component and root cause
   - Progressive damage, if applicable
   - Technician diagnosis/report
   - Work order and repair location
   - Coverage, Claim Type, and covered labor/parts percentages

3. **Verify coverage**
   Confirm coverage for the specific unit and component in QuickServe, PGBU, Guidanz, or applicable warranty documentation. Do not use the build date as the warranty start date or assume every component is covered.

4. **Prepare the claim in BMS**
   Enter and validate the required fields, including:
   - Routing, application, pay, and Claim Type codes
   - Serial number, failure code/date, hours or mileage
   - Unit information and all four C sections
   - SRT, labor, parts, and charge allocations

5. **Complete and verify**
   - Open **Total Claim** and select **Complete**.
   - Correct any BMS errors.

### When Stop Work Authority Applies / Quand arrêter le travail

Examples include:

- Environmental or biological hazards, including rodent contamination.
- Unsafe access to the generator or work area.
- Unsafe ladders, unstable ground, missing guardrails, or inadequate fall protection.
- Significant snow or ice preventing safe access.
- A customer requesting work despite unsafe conditions.
- A customer refusing required Lock Out / Tag Out (LOTO).
- Working alone when the task requires a second technician for safety.

Exemples :

- Risques environnementaux ou biologiques, incluant la présence de rongeurs ou d'excréments.
- Accès non sécuritaire à la génératrice ou à la zone de travail.
- Échelle non sécuritaire, sol instable, garde-corps absent ou protection contre les chutes inadéquate.
- Neige ou glace importante empêchant un accès sécuritaire.
- Client demandant de poursuivre les travaux malgré une condition dangereuse.
- Client refusant une procédure de cadenassage (LOTO) requise.
- Travail seul lorsqu'un deuxième technicien est requis pour assurer la sécurité.

# Customers - Generator Does Not Start During a Power Outage

# Last Updated: 2026-09-03

## Purpose

This procedure provides Service Coordinators with a simple troubleshooting workflow to guide customers whose generator does not automatically start during a utility power outage and especially during after-hours where sending a technician out to help implies overtime rates.

The objective is to determine whether the issue can be resolved through basic operator actions before dispatching a technician in regular day-hours rather than after-hours.

> **Important**
>
> This procedure is intended for basic customer troubleshooting only.
>
> This procedure is intended for Cummins/Onan generators only.
>
> Customers should never perform work that exposes them to electrical hazards or unsafe conditions.
>
> If at any point the customer is uncomfortable performing a step, discontinue the procedure and schedule service.

## Objectif

Cette procédure fournit aux coordonnateurs de service un flux de dépannage simple pour guider les clients dont le générateur ne démarre pas automatiquement lors d'une panne de courant du réseau électrique, en particulier en dehors des heures normales, où l'envoi d'un technicien implique des tarifs de temps supplémentaire.

L'objectif est de déterminer si le problème peut être résolu par des actions de base de l'opérateur avant de dépêcher un technicien pendant les heures normales de la journée plutôt qu'en dehors des heures normales.

> **Important**
>
> Cette procédure est destinée uniquement au dépannage de base par le client.
>
> Cette procédure est destinée uniquement aux générateurs Cummins/Onan.
>
> Les clients ne doivent jamais effectuer de travaux les exposant à des risques électriques ou à des conditions dangereuses.
>
> Si, à tout moment, le client se sent mal à l'aise d'exécuter une étape, interrompre la procédure et planifier une intervention de service.

Arrange for a Cummins Service technician.

# Information to Collect Before Dispatch

If a technician will be dispatched, collect as much information as possible from the customer.

Recommended information includes:

- Active fault code
- Alarm description
- Whether the generator started manually
- Whether the reset procedure was attempted
- Any unusual observations

Examples:

- Low Coolant
- High Engine Temperature
- FC1223
- Emergency Stop active

This information assists the Service Coordinator in selecting the appropriate technician and preparing the service call.

---

# Safety Reminders

Advise the customer to stop the procedure immediately if:

- Smoke is present.
- Fire is present.
- Fuel is leaking.
- Electrical hazards are observed.
- The generator appears unsafe to operate.

In these situations:

- Do not continue troubleshooting.
- Arrange for immediate service.

---

# Best Practices

- Record any fault codes before scheduling service.
- Walk through each troubleshooting step in order.
- Keep the customer informed throughout the process.
- Escalate the call if the generator cannot be safely restarted.

---

# Common Mistakes

## Selector Not Left in AUTO

A generator cannot automatically respond to a power outage unless the controller is left in **AUTO** mode.

---

## Alarm Reset Skipped

Always attempt a basic alarm reset before proceeding to manual start when an alarm is present.

---

## Repeated Start Attempts

Repeatedly attempting to start the generator without identifying the underlying fault may worsen the situation.

If the generator does not start after the basic procedure, schedule service.

---

## Missing Fault Information

Whenever possible, record any displayed alarm or fault code before dispatching a technician.

This information greatly improves troubleshooting efficiency.

results.question: A hospital generator is down, the ATS failed, the generator is running manually, and the site is on the South Shore. As a coordinator, what information should I confirm, what type of technician should I look for, and what should I do before dispatch?

run.answer:
Treat this as a **Priority 1 critical-site ATS failure**.

### Confirm
- Exact South Shore location and site access/contact details.
- Utility power status and whether the hospital load is currently stable.
- Generator operating condition in manual mode.
- ATS model, alarms, position, and failure symptoms.
- Whether an outage/transfer simulation is permitted.
- Whether hospital personnel must participate and approve switching.
- Any prior repair attempts or recurring issues.

### Technician profile
Select the **closest available field technician qualified in ATS and generator controls**, preferably familiar with the site. ATS preference order:

1. François Racine  
2. Christian Dubreuil  
3. Alain Duguay  
4. Ali Reza-Sabour  
5. Kevin Duranceau  

Kevin is a qualified South Shore field technician with ATS/control capability, but availability and proximity must still be checked.

### Before dispatch
- Confirm outage-simulation availability.
- Arrange required hospital/customer participation.
- Clearly advise the technician that the generator is running manually and the ATS has failed.
- Verify technician availability, travel time, qualifications, and customer commitments.
- Do not interrupt the current manual supply without site authorization and an approved switching plan.

*Based on the Cummins technician-selection rules and profiles; site-safety details are general operational guidance.*

- The generator appears unsafe to operate.

## Selector Not Left in AUTO

A generator cannot automatically respond to a power outage unless the controller is left in **AUTO** mode.

## Alarm Reset Skipped

Always attempt a basic alarm reset before proceeding to manual start when an alarm is present.

---

## Repeated Start Attempts

Repeatedly attempting to start the generator without identifying the underlying fault may worsen the situation.

If the generator does not start after the basic procedure, schedule service.

Whenever possible, record any displayed alarm or fault code before dispatching a technician.

results.question: An airport has no current outage, but preventive maintenance is overdue and the customer has a service window. How should I prepare this service call before assigning and confirming a technician?

run.answer:
Before technician assignment, prepare it as a **preventive-maintenance job**, not an outage call:

1. **Confirm scope and urgency**
   - Verify the generator can currently start and carry load.
   - Record how overdue the PM is and how many times it has been rescheduled.
   - Each reschedule raises PM priority one level; after two reschedules, further postponement requires supervisor approval. PM cannot exceed P3.

2. **Confirm customer requirements**
   - Verify the airport’s account, PM contract, and covered work.
   - Document the approved service window and applicable customer authorization.
   - Confirm parts/material availability; do not schedule work dependent on unavailable parts without approval.

3. **Document site requirements**
   - On-site contact and telephone number.
   - Airport security, parking, gate, escort, badging, access, and safety restrictions.
   - Equipment location and whether an accessible site representative/network will be available.

4. **Verify equipment details**
   - Manufacturer, model, serial number, operating hours, and unit location.
   - Record any active alarms, leaks, battery issues, or other symptoms.

5. **Prepare BMS/FieldAware**
   - Associate the correct unit and site.
   - Use **SOLUTIONS** if covered by a PM contract; otherwise **STANDBY**.
   - Set Primary Failure Measure to **HOURS** and enter the latest reading.
   - Include scope, service window, access instructions, billing/coverage status, required reports, and supporting documents.

Then complete the pre-assignment review and select a technician who can meet the approved airport access window and job requirements.

# Alarm Classification

## Purpose

An alarm or fault does **not** have an intrinsic priority.

Its urgency is determined by its **impact on the availability of the equipment**, not simply by the alarm code itself.

The dispatcher must determine how the alarm affects the generator before assigning a priority.

---

# Alarm Levels

| Alarm Level | Definition | Typical Priority |
|--------------|------------|------------------|
| **Blocking Alarm** | The generator cannot start or cannot accept load. Examples include active shutdowns, failed start attempts, ATS transfer failures, or any condition that makes the unit unavailable. | **P1** for C1–C2 customers without redundancy or with safety impact; **P2** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Reliability Alarm** | The generator continues to operate but its ability to support a future outage is compromised. Examples include battery charger failures, low fuel level, defective block heater, coolant leak, etc. | **P2** for C1–C2 customers; **P3** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Minor Alarm** | No immediate impact on equipment availability. Examples include sensor faults, reminder lamps, or maintenance notifications. | Service Call (Non-Urgent): **P3** (C1–C3) or **P5** (C4). |

---

# Dispatcher Decision Process

The primary question is:

> **If utility power fails right now, will the generator start and carry the load?**

| Answer | Alarm Classification |
|---------|----------------------|
| No, or uncertain | Blocking Alarm |
| Yes, but with increased risk | Reliability Alarm |
| Yes, with no significant risk | Minor Alarm |

This single question should guide the initial classification before determining the final priority.

---

# Additional Considerations

Alarm classification should also consider the probability that the equipment could fail before the next maintenance opportunity.

Factors may include:

- Oil pressure
- Engine temperature
- Fuel level
- Battery condition
- Coolant leaks
- Site redundancy
- Whether the entire facility depends on the generator
- Criticality of the customer's operation

The coordinator should ask enough questions to determine whether the generator is:

- Completely shut down (`Shutdown`)
- Operating with reduced reliability (`Warning`)
- Operating normally with only informational notifications

---

# Typical Shutdown Conditions

A preventive maintenance activity that reaches **P3** becomes equivalent to a typical non-urgent service call but never reaches the priority of an equipment failure.

Once a PM has been rescheduled twice, it may not be postponed again without supervisor approval.

Each reschedule increases the priority by one level. No preventive maintenance activity should be postponed more than two times.

---

## Rule 5 — Customer Ranking

When two jobs have the same Priority Level and the same Client Class, customer ranking is used as the final business tie-breaker.

Use this report when a user asks for the best, top, or highest-ranked customers/clients, particularly when customer sales or margin ranking is being used as a dispatch tie-breaker.

Customer ranking is based on the organization's sales and margin classification.

# Bank of Canada — Security Access

## Purpose

This procedure explains the security screening process that must be completed for an employee or technician who requires access to a **Bank of Canada (BoC) site**.

Bank of Canada security screening is separate from security clearances obtained for other government buildings. An employee who is already cleared to enter another government facility **cannot use that clearance as authorization to access a Bank of Canada site**.

---

## Source Document

The complete Bank of Canada security screening instructions are available here:

**Source document:** [Bank of Canada Security Screening Instructions](https://cummins365-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/ud016_cummins_com/IQAT5Bccq0NaSoMAFkOsofWaARmvZBsF5YEdpQFG0mErnaU?e=FqD2u4)

---

## Security Screening Process

### 1. Personal Information Request (PIR)

A **Personal Information Request (PIR)** form will be sent to the employer or employee requiring access.

The individual requiring access must:

1. Complete the PIR form.
2. Send the completed form to:
   **facilities-RFA@bank-banque-canada.ca**
3. Include:
   - the Bank of Canada site location for which access is required;
   - the expected frequency of access.

---

### 2. Mintz Screening Invitation

After the PIR has been submitted, allow **up to 48 hours** to receive the Mintz screening invitation.

The Mintz invitation may be delivered to the employee's **spam or junk folder**, so these folders should be checked if the invitation does not appear in the main inbox.

If no Mintz invitation has been received within 48 hours, including in spam/junk folders, contact:

**facilities-RFA@bank-banque-canada.ca**

for assistance.

### Important — Mintz Expiration

The Mintz invitation must be completed **within 10 days of receiving it**.

If it is not completed within 10 days, the invitation will be cancelled and a **new Mintz submission will be required**.

---

### 3. Fingerprints — If Requested

After passing the Mintz screening, the employee may be asked to provide fingerprints to assist with identification.

If fingerprints are required:

1. The employee will receive an email containing a **Commissionaires fingerprint request form**.
2. Bring the request form to a **Commissionaires office** in the employee's area.
3. Complete the fingerprint process.
4. The Commissionaires will provide a document after the fingerprints have been taken.
5. Send this document to:

**facilities-RFA@bank-banque-canada.ca**

Fingerprints are therefore **not automatically required for every applicant**. They are completed when requested as part of the screening process.

---

### 4. Phone Interview — If Requested

Depending on the findings of the Mintz screening, the employee may also be asked to complete a **phone interview**.

The interview normally lasts approximately **5–10 minutes**, depending on the situation.

---

### 5. Declaration Kit

After all required Mintz processes have been completed, the employee will receive a **Declaration Kit**.

The employee must:

1. Sign all fields highlighted in yellow.
2. Obtain the required witness authorization signature.

The witness:

- cannot be the employee;
- may be a coworker, family member, or friend;
- must be **over 18 years old**.

---

### 6. Employee Headshot

A headshot of the employee must be submitted with the signed Declaration Kit.

The headshot must have a **white background**.

Send the headshot as an attachment in the **same email as the signed Declaration Kit**.

---

### 7. Security Profile and Site Access

Once all required screening steps have been completed, allow **up to 48 hours** for:

- the employee's Bank of Canada security profile to be completed; and
- the requested site access to be linked to the employee's BOC security profile.

Once this process is complete, the employee may access the identified Bank of Canada site.

---

## Security Access Renewal

The Bank of Canada monitors the expiry dates of technician security access.

The personal email address is used to communicate with the CNL Security Personnel team and to send system updates to the worker.

---

## 6. Who Is the CNL Contractor Representative?

The **CNL Contractor Representative** is the CNL employee responsible for the contractors while they are working at a CNL site.

This person is normally someone associated with the project or a construction superintendent.

The Company SPOC must know who the CNL Contractor Representative is **before submitting the onboarding request**.

---

## 7. What Information Is Needed From the CNL Contractor Representative?

Certain information is required when submitting an onboarding request.

The Company SPOC must know:

- whether the worker is required to be a **Nuclear Energy Worker**;
- whether **bioassay** is required for the worker;
- what **security level** is required.

> For the Cummins-specific values used when onboarding technicians, refer to the **CNL Access and Compliance** procedure.

---

## 8. What Happens After the Onboarding Request Is Submitted?

After submission, the **CNL Contractor Representative** must approve or reject the request.

The Company SPOC should ensure the Contractor Representative knows that a request has been submitted so that it can be reviewed promptly.

Once the Contractor Representative approves the request, it is sent to the **CNL Personnel Security team** to begin the security screening process.

---

## 9. What Is the Worker Required to Do?

The worker receives **two emails** from the ServiceCNL system:

- one containing their username;
- one containing their password.

The worker must use these credentials to log into the system and begin completing their assigned tasks.

> **Important:** Tasks should be completed as soon as possible. The request may be cancelled if there is no activity.

## 10. Does the Company SPOC Receive Notifications?

Yes.

The Company SPOC can monitor updates for each onboarding request through the **ServiceCNL dashboard**.

The Company SPOC will also receive **email updates throughout the process**.

## 11. What Other Tasks Must the Worker Complete?

results.question: Help. A customer reports an intermittent PCC3300 alarm after a breaker transfer while an ATS transitions under load. What do I need to clarify before deciding what to do or dispatching a technician?

run.answer:
Before deciding priority or dispatch, clarify:

### Alarm and event
- Is **PCC3300 the controller model**, or is there an actual fault/alarm code?
- Exact alarm text/code, status, timestamp, and event-log sequence.
- Is the alarm active, latched, or already cleared?
- Which breaker transferred, in which direction, and during what ATS transition?
- Does it occur every transfer or intermittently? **Do not ask the customer to recreate it under load.**

### Current equipment availability
Ask the key prioritization question:

> If utility power fails now, will the generator start, transfer, and carry the load?

Also confirm:
- Generator starts manually and runs normally.
- ATS is in AUTO and indicates normal source positions.
- Generator can accept/carry load.
- Any failed transfer, shutdown, outage, abnormal voltage/frequency, or load interruption.
- Site redundancy and customer criticality.

### Equipment/site details
- Generator, controller, ATS model and serial numbers.
- Open-, delayed-, or closed-transition ATS, if known.
- Recent service, programming changes, breaker work, or commissioning.
- Available screenshots, event logs, and ATS/controller fault history.
- Current load level when the event occurred.

### Safety
Ask about smoke, fire, fuel leaks, arcing, overheating, or exposed electrical hazards. If present, stop troubleshooting and arrange immediate service.

### Initial classification
- Cannot start, transfer, or carry load—or uncertain: **Blocking alarm**
- Still operational but future transfer reliability is compromised: **Reliability alarm**
- No meaningful availability impact: **Minor alarm**

Final priority then depends on customer criticality and redundancy. Dispatch should likely require ATS/generator-controls capability, but the provided technician profiles do not establish PCC3300-specific qualification.

# Alarm Classification

## Purpose

An alarm or fault does **not** have an intrinsic priority.

Its urgency is determined by its **impact on the availability of the equipment**, not simply by the alarm code itself.

The dispatcher must determine how the alarm affects the generator before assigning a priority.

---

# Alarm Levels

| Alarm Level | Definition | Typical Priority |
|--------------|------------|------------------|
| **Blocking Alarm** | The generator cannot start or cannot accept load. Examples include active shutdowns, failed start attempts, ATS transfer failures, or any condition that makes the unit unavailable. | **P1** for C1–C2 customers without redundancy or with safety impact; **P2** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Reliability Alarm** | The generator continues to operate but its ability to support a future outage is compromised. Examples include battery charger failures, low fuel level, defective block heater, coolant leak, etc. | **P2** for C1–C2 customers; **P3** for C3–C4 customers. |
| **Minor Alarm** | No immediate impact on equipment availability. Examples include sensor faults, reminder lamps, or maintenance notifications. | Service Call (Non-Urgent): **P3** (C1–C3) or **P5** (C4). |

---

# Dispatcher Decision Process

The primary question is:

> **If utility power fails right now, will the generator start and carry the load?**

| Answer | Alarm Classification |
|---------|----------------------|
| No, or uncertain | Blocking Alarm |
| Yes, but with increased risk | Reliability Alarm |
| Yes, with no significant risk | Minor Alarm |

This single question should guide the initial classification before determining the final priority.

---

# Additional Considerations

Alarm classification should also consider the probability that the equipment could fail before the next maintenance opportunity.

Factors may include:

- Oil pressure
- Engine temperature
- Fuel level
- Battery condition
- Coolant leaks
- Site redundancy
- Whether the entire facility depends on the generator
- Criticality of the customer's operation

The coordinator should ask enough questions to determine whether the generator is:

- Completely shut down (`Shutdown`)
- Operating with reduced reliability (`Warning`)
- Operating normally with only informational notifications

# FieldAware - Work Order Creation and Scheduling

# Last Updated: 2026-09-03

## Purpose

Use [BMS - Work Order Creation](bms_work_order_creation.md) for creating and updating the BMS Work Order and synchronizing it with FieldAware.

## Objectif

Consultez [BMS - Work Order Creation](bms_work_order_creation.md) pour créer et modifier le bon de travail dans BMS et le synchroniser avec FieldAware.

# 1. Synchronize the BMS Work Order

Before opening FieldAware, confirm that the BMS Work Order is complete and saved.

Select:

```text
Send to FA
```

Use **Send to FA** again after every material BMS change. Unsynchronized changes may be overwritten when the technician updates the job.

The **FA Job ID** is generated or displayed after synchronization. Record it for the FieldAware search and related paperwork.

# 2. Open the FieldAware Job

1. Complete the product-specific unit information.
2. Confirm the application and configuration values.
3. Return to the **Failure** tab.
4. Add the applicable Claim Type if BMS did not populate it automatically.
5. Use **Build Cause Narrative** when available to generate the Cause text.
6. Confirm that the narrative accurately reflects the technician's report.

## Multiple Claims on One Work Order

When multiple claims are recorded on the same Work Order, additional allocation and claim-management steps may apply. Follow the applicable multi-claim procedure before completing the invoice.

## Final Pre-Submission Check

Verify the Routing Code, Engine Serial Number or unit serial number, Application Code, Pay Code, Claim Type, Failure Code, failure date, hours or mileage, and the required 4 C documentation. Then continue with the SRT, labor, parts, and charge-allocation procedures.

## Résumé en français

Avant de créer la réclamation, vérifier l’unité, le numéro de série, la date de début de garantie, les heures ou le kilométrage, la pièce défectueuse, la cause, le code de défaillance et le type de travail. Dans BMS, remplir les onglets **Warranty**, **Claim**, **Unit** et **Failure** avec les valeurs propres à la garantie concernée. Les codes de compte et les indicateurs de routage doivent être confirmés avant l’envoi.
